prerequisites: Basic familiarity as a common user with a computer.

learning_outcomes.text: Basic knowledge on the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases and computer programs with application in engineering.
Locate computer science within engineering disciplines.
Understand the fundamentals of the binary system to comprehend information representation in computers.
Identify the hardware components that constitute a computer system, as well as their interconnection in networks, and understand their basic functioning.
Distinguish the main peripherals used in a computer system and specifically in the field of engineering.
Classify the different types of software used in a computer system.
Identify and classify different types of computer systems and their application areas.
Know the main functions performed by an operating system.
Analyze what services the operating system provides to programs and end-users.
Identify the main operating systems used in professional engineering environments and utilize the main services at a user level.
Know the main functions performed by a database management system.
Create data models for simple problems.
Use basic expressions to retrieve and modify information stored in a database.
Identify which database management systems are used in professional engineering environments.
Identify the main application programs used in professional engineering environments.
Understand the concept of an algorithm and the process of abstracting a problem in programming.
Identify the program development process and its location within the general Software Engineering process.
Recognize the elemental data structures provided by a structured programming language.
Manage the elemental control structures of a structured programming language.
Abstract operations.
Design small applications to solve elementary problems in collaborative work environments.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: Overview of computer science in the context of other engineering disciplines
Introduction: Structure and functioning of a computer
Introduction: Representation of information in a computer
Introduction to databases: Concept of database
Introduction to databases: Fundamentals of the relational data model
Introduction to databases: Performing queries and modifications
Introduction to databases: Database Management Systems in professional engineering environments
Introduction to programming: Abstraction of problems for programming: fundamental concepts
Introduction to programming: Variables, expressions, assignment
Introduction to programming: Use of console input/output
Introduction to programming: Handling basic flow control structures: sequential, alternative, and repetitive
Introduction to programming: Definition and use of subprograms and functions. Variable scope
Introduction to programming: File input/output
Introduction to programming: Basic data types and structures
Introduction to programming: Program development processes. From high-level to execution on the processor. Compiled languages and interpreted languages
Hardware and software components of a computer system: Structure and functioning of a computer: Von Neumann Architecture and machine language
Hardware and software components of a computer system: Peripheral devices
Hardware and software components of a computer system: System interconnection: types, mechanisms, and applications
Hardware and software components of a computer system: Types of software: base software and application software
Hardware and software components of a computer system: Types of computer systems and their application areas
Introduction to operating systems: Concept and functions performed by an operating system
Introduction to operating systems: Interface and services offered to programs
Introduction to operating systems: Interface and services offered to users
Introduction to operating systems: Operating systems used in professional engineering environments
Introduction to laboratory tools. The spreadsheet as a tool (4h)
Database design, implementation, and exploitation (6h)
Programming with Python: Introduction to the development environment (18h)
Programming with Python: Variables, expressions, and console input-output (18h)
Programming with Python: Flow control: if-else, while, for (18h)
Programming with Python: Functions (18h)
Programming with Python: Structures: lists and strings (18h)
Programming with Python: Files (18h)

assessment_methods.method: Theoretical exam (Theme 4 - Hardware and Software Components)
Theoretical exam (Theme 5 - Introduction to Operating Systems)
Practical exam (P1 - The spreadsheet as a tool)
Practical exam (P2 - Database design, implementation and exploitation)

assessment_rules: For the theoretical block, if less than 40% of the total score in Theme 3 is obtained, the block is not passed. A score greater than 4 out of 10 is required for the theoretical block to average with the practical block. For the practical block, if less than 40% of the total score in Theme 3 (P3) is obtained, the block is not passed. A score greater than 4 out of 10 is required for the practical block to average with the theoretical block. The final grade is calculated as 0.5 * Theoretical Grade + 0.5 * Practical Grade. If minimums are not met, the final grade will be the minimum of the calculated grade and 4.0. For the extraordinary examination, the minimum passing grade for each block to average is 5 out of 10, and grades of 5.0 or higher from the ordinary examination can be carried over.
